Why would the IANA be a meson option and not something we get from entity-manager?

The thought was that BMC update today is a singleton already (i.e. bmcweb hard codes the association on lookup, iirc). I had a patch for getting it from entity-manager, but moved to this because the runtime path is simpler, and we didn't seem to sacrifice much for it.
Am I missing usecases where we can't set it through meson options (i.e. we can't know the identifiers at build) or do you have a preference for entity-manager?

> Am I missing usecases where we can't set it through meson options (i.e. we can't know the identifiers at build) or do you have a preference for entity-manager?

I guess I don't have a lot of skin in this decision.

I don't know if you have any cases where you want to restrict the image to be updated based on the EEPROM detection of the hardware.  IBM does some stuff where they have a minimal device tree and then they do some detection and load a more robust device tree.  Maybe that's still all one image.

If you have image A1 -> An, then using the image settings (via Meson config) is fine.  If you have image A1 -> Bn, where they're not identical in IANA, you'd need EEPROM data to be able to do that.

Generally, I like having it in the entity-manager data just because that's where we have all the other IANA information and I don't like the proliferation of meson options, but it isn't a hard requirement.

That's fair, I can definitely understand wanting uniformity. If we want to go with entity-manager just to avoid exceptions in how we define this, I'm fine with that. 

For the An -> Bn, its not clear to me what situation you'd run into where this wouldn't work, its very possible I'm just being dense. If you changed device identifiers across a firmware boundary, you're going to run into a situation where you'd need to build a new fwpkg with both sets of descriptors to transition cleanly across that boundary, no? or just build a new version of An with the new device identifiers. In any case, you won't have to deal with incompatibility at update time, just after it boots, at which point you'd have to have a new package anyways to match the new identifiers.

i.e. if you're on image A, with device identifiers x and y, you can still build a fwpkg where the image being updated to will report z and c. But after update you can't update back to image A without also packaging device descriptors support for x and y, or rebuilding the binary into a "transitory package". Its not clear to me how having this in entity-manager mitigates this problem. Are you saying that people may want to be able to advertise what device descriptors they support based off of which eeprom they find, i.e. one image for any number of actual configurations, but they are advertising it under different device descriptors based on eeprom (maybe off of product_sku, for example)?

> For the An -> Bn, its not clear to me what situation you'd run into where this wouldn't work, its very possible I'm just being dense.

Currently you have a single string as "compatible hardware", which implies to me that this image is only going to accept a single image type that it has been programmed to accept ("An").

I could see designs where you have a single DC-SCM type (A) but that DC-SCM goes into multiple platforms (B, C).  You program "A" at your DC-SCM manufacturing, which is some generic image type, and then during your chassis build you plug the card into a "B" chassis and want to program it with the "B" image.  If the Entity-Manager compatible for some FRU in the chassis says "compatible with com.company.BMC.B" then this repository can accept transitioning from "An" to "Bn".  But if you go the meson route, as I'm interpreting it, you can't do this kind of transition because the "An" image will say "I only accept com.company.BMC.A images".
Thanks for the explanation, I agree with you. I'll change it to take compatible from entity manager.
Done and updated, thank you for your feedback.

Is this ROTless or rootless?
ROTless. this is really just "self update," i.e. update via cp to /run/initramfs and reboot.
Done

We generally want all options `enabled` in CI.  Having it be disabled means we have code that isn't even compile-tested in CI.

Are we comfortable that the code between the two of them is minimal enough that it is acceptable to have only one path compiled?

Most of the code is under an ifconstexpr, so it will at least have syntactic checking. That said, I'm fine with having it enabled in CI. I'm open to feedback on how to deal with this in general, but I didn't love having compile time code switches, this just seemed to be the least invasive change and the least risky way to introduce this change. That said, it will have a PACKAGECONFIG switch in yocto anyways, so not sure there's much actual risk to have this default to enabled.

There is no such approved design for this flow. BMCWeb will support only single Multipart update interface. Please raise a design update for https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/code-update.md for approval first.
Please make sure any further design updates are aligned on discussion here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76645/comment/39e9183c_afc771dd/.

> There is no such approved design for this flow. BMCWeb will support only single Multipart update interface.

I'm not understanding this comment.  The flow proposed here still supports multipart.

> Please raise a design update for https://github.com/openbmc/docs/blob/master/designs/code-update.md for approval first.
> Please make sure any further design updates are aligned on discussion here https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/docs/+/76645/comment/39e9183c_afc771dd/.

bmcweb -> bmc-code-updater is the only flow that's changing here, and the DBus api itself isn't changing.  Is there a design concern that you'd like to see addressed?  Ideally if you could outline a requirement that you think this doesn't handle we could have a productive conversation.  From my perspective, this is a pretty minimal changeset, so if I were writing Marcs design doc, I'm not sure what I'd put in it.
